transcript:
Header: 2026-09-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: 00:46:00 | Recording started
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM); Samir Patel (BlueHarbor Head of Security), Laura Kim (Procurement), Derek Owens (Platform Lead), Nina Rao (Legal)

Summary: quick intake to understand procurement gates, legal and security requirements for onboarding Redwood. BlueHarbor is evaluating vendor that can meet financial services data residency and encryption reqs, wants clarity on SLAs and pricing approval timeline.

[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick round intro, im jamie, im the account exec, uh ethan is our se and maya will be on CSM; blueharbor could you intro yourselves?
[00:10] Samir: samir here, head of security, we own controls and audits, mainly curious about SOC 2 and key management, also very sensitive to data residency, we have eu and us customers so need region separation
[00:22] Laura: laura, procurement manager, i'll own the purchase order and vendor intake, we have a standard packet we send to finance and legal, want to understand any non-negotiable clauses in your MSA
[00:33] Derek: derek, platform lead, interested in perf, latency, and how tenant isolation looks for a multi-tenant hosted model vs dedicated capacity
[00:40] Nina: nina from legal, i'll be reviewing DPA redlines and anything on indemnity/sgc, subcontractors, audits
[00:46] Jamie: great, thanks. to set expectations this meeting is mostly intake; we can share docs after, and we typically run a short pilot to validate perf and cost.

[01:05] Ethan: on the technical side, Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private/vpc deployments. For regulated workloads most folks either go Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and data isolation on reserved GPU pools, while Private is customer-managed networking for air-gapped or VPC-only setups.

[01:24] Derek: can you clarify isolation on Dedicated? like if we spin up a pool for BlueHarbor is it logically isolated or do you have co-tenancy?
[01:30] Ethan: dedicated pools are single-tenant at the pool level — no other customers share those GPUs; control plane still runs in our managed plane, but data in flight and at rest can be encrypted and we support customer KMS in Private, for Dedicated we offer KMS integration via customer-managed keys in specific regions.

[01:51] Samir: when you say KMS integration what exactly — do you store keys? where are they stored and do you support HSM-backed keys?
[01:56] Ethan: good q. for hosted we currently offer envelope encryption where keys are rotated via a Redwood-managed KMS; for Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and optionally HSM-backed keys depending on the cloud customer config. for Private we don't hold keys — customer provides KMS and all keys stay in their account.

[02:21] Nina: about subcontractors and subprocessors, can you list where your compute is run and whether you use third-party infra providers? we need to be explicit in the DPA.
[02:29] Jamie: yes we'll include a subprocessors list in the security packet. redwood runs on major cloud providers in regions we support; for Dedicated customers we can provision in a specific region and include that in the subcontractor list.

[02:40] Laura: procurement process question — finance will need a cadence for invoicing and PO acceptance. do you invoice monthly and do you accept net-30? also any minimum commitments for Dedicated?
[02:49] Maya: invoicing is flexible; hosted customers are pay-as-you-go, we do monthly invoices. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits; minimums depend on the size of the pool but we can surface options. we support net-30 via standard terms and can accept PO numbers on invoices.

[03:10] Samir: SLA targets — we need 99.9% availability for inference endpoints and clear SLOs for latency. do you have enterprise SLAs?
[03:18] Jamie: yes enterprise SLAs are available for Dedicated and Private with uptime guarantees and financial credits. typical target is 99.9 for API availability on Dedicated with escalation paths. we'll include the SLA doc and the exceptions list.

[03:34] Derek: can you share telemetry and observability hooks? we need token-level cost, per-route tracing, and export of audit logs to our SIEM.
[03:42] Ethan: Redwood Console exposes per-route metrics, token-level breakdowns, trace logs. we can stream audit logs to a customer S3 or SIEM via connector, and we maintain an audit trail. we'll include sample log schemas.

[04:05] Nina: indemnity and liability caps — our legal team will likely ask for limits and carve-outs for gross negligence; we need to understand your standard positions so we can flag anything that needs escalation.
[04:15] Jamie: standard MSA has a liability cap tied to fees paid in prior 12 months; we can share the MSA and point out negotiable vs non-negotiable items.

[04:30] Laura: timeline — we can't start procurement until we have the DPA and SOC2 report; what's realistic?
[04:36] Jamie: we can provide SOC2 summary and security docs same week; formal SOC2 report under NDA typically. DPA redlines we can accept a few reasonable changes, and we aim to have procurement paperwork in 2-3 weeks given parallel legal review.

[04:50] Samir: data residency question — can you guarantee EU-only processing for EU customer data?
[04:56] Ethan: yes, for Dedicated and Private we can pin capacity in EU regions. For hosted multi-tenant we route to regional endpoints where available, but if strict EU-only processing is required we recommend Dedicated or Private so we can enforce region isolation.

[05:12] Derek: about performance — we will provide a representative prompt set, can you run a benchmark that mirrors our 512-token seqs and concurrent QPS?
[05:20] Ethan: absolutely, if you share sample workload and a small test dataset we will run latency and throughput runs, include KV cache/continuous batching configs, and share per-token cost estimates.

[05:34] Nina: regarding DPA: we have a strict subcontractor clause and need to ensure there's notification before onboarding new subprocessors and a right to audit or object. how do you handle that?
[05:44] Jamie: we provide a subprocessors list and give notice when adding materially different subprocessors; contractual audit rights are limited but we support SOC2 and virtual audits for enterprise customers under NDA. we'll provide our standard language and where possible flag negotiation points.

[06:00] Laura: price approvals — our procurement approvals thread a pricing committee for annual commitments above a certain threshold. who owns pricing exceptions?
[06:08] Maya: that's handled by AE and revenue ops; we can provide a pricing approval sheet and typical discount bands by commit level. we'll note anything outside standard bands for escalation.

[06:22] Samir: encryption at rest? are data and KV caches encrypted? what about ephemeral GPU memory?
[06:29] Ethan: data at rest is encrypted; KV cache persisted stores are encrypted and we can enable customer-managed KMS for Dedicated or Private. ephemeral memory on GPUs is not persisted but we treat it as protected runtime — for the strictest compliance we recommend Private with air-gapped deployment.

[06:48] Derek: what about model weights or derivative data — do you retain any training or logs of prompts used?
[06:54] Jamie: by default we do not use customer data for model training; retention policies can be configured and we can include deletion windows in the DPA. logs and prompts used for inference are retained per retention settings and can be exported or purged on request.

[07:12] Nina: we will want language on data deletion and timelines in DPA plus certification that you won't use data to improve models.
[07:19] Ethan: we will include explicit non-training clauses for enterprise accounts and configurable retention policies.

[07:30] Laura: acceptance criteria — finance needs a channel to escalate billing disputes and dispute SLAs.
[07:36] Maya: our billing team has a dedicated mailbox and we will provide escalation contacts; disputes are typically handled in 30 days.

[07:45] Jamie: quick note on pricing — pilot pricing for dedicated capacity is often offered as a short-term commit with pilot discount; once production we move to reserved pricing. we can propose a pilot pricing sheet with options.

[07:58] Derek: do you have references in financial services? we prefer vendors who've done regulated workloads
[08:03] Jamie: yes we have a handful of FS customers, we'll include anonymized reference contacts in the packet.

[08:20] Samir: about SSO and RBAC — we need SAML-based SSO and granular role controls for developer vs admin.
[08:27] Ethan: we support SAML and OIDC, fine-grained RBAC in the Console, and can integrate with your identity provider for SSO and SCIM for provisioning.

[08:40] Nina: on audits — do you support evidence collection for controls and can you share a list of mapped controls to SOC2?
[08:47] Jamie: yes we'll provide a controls matrix mapping our controls to common frameworks and will provide SOC2 summary under NDA.

[09:00] Laura: procurement gate question — is there an onboarding kickoff? we typically want a technical onboarding and a security review before contracts sign.
[09:06] Maya: onboarding kickoff is standard once PO is issued; we can do a security deep-dive and operational runbook session as part of onboarding.

[09:20] Derek: network connectivity — are there egress IP lists or do you support customer IP allowlists for calls to your endpoints?
[09:26] Ethan: we support IP allowlisting, and for Dedicated/Private we can provide static egress IPs and VPC peering options.

[09:40] Samir: compliance with EU data protection — do you have any model-specific leakage concerns, e.g., models caching prompts across sessions?
[09:47] Ethan: our runtime uses session-specific KV caches and we have options to isolate prefix caches by customer; we do not share KV caches across tenants. we'll include technical notes on cache isolation.

[09:58] Jamie: ok let me recap and make sure we have alignment: we'll send the MSA/DPA and security packet including subprocessors list and SOC2 summary; ethan will run bench once blueharbor shares workload; laura will share procurement form and po template; nina will flag DPA items to escalate. schedule pilot kickoff week of 9/22 if that works.

[10:20] Nina: sounds good, i'll start initial redlines on DPA and prioritize subcontractor and data deletion clauses.
[10:27] Laura: i'll share procurement cadence and our finance lead contact for PO issuance.
[10:31] Derek: we'll prepare the sample workload and QPS profile for the benchmark.
[10:35] Samir: please include details on key rotation and HSM support in the packet.
[10:40] Jamie: will do. thanks everyone.

[10:45] -- Meeting End --

Notes: transcript contains occasional partial timestamps, speaker overlap and some transcription artifacts (names sometimes mis-heard). Packet to include: MSA clean copy, DPA, SOC2 summary (NDA), subprocessors list, SLA doc, pricing pilot sheet, sample log schema, reference list.
